extracted.intended_audience: students and theorists of comedy, dramatists, playwrights, literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical framework for understanding what makes things comic and how to create comic characters/types for drama and literature, contrasting comic methods with tragic ones and detailing functions of laughter. Focuses on observation methods, comic traits (esp. vanity), professional/jargon-based comedy, and the special kind of absurdity involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy aims at the general
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is the only art that aims at the general; its subject-matter is generality itself (types/classes) rather than unique individuals, so the generality lies in the work itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with tragedy (which aims at individuality). Examples: classical comedy titles like Le Misanthrope, l'Avare, le Joueur indicate whole classes of people; comic poets often give multiple secondary characters as simplified copies of a central prototype. Use of plural/collective titles (Les Femmes savantes) signals this tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy lies midway between art and life and performs a corrective social function
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy accepts social life as a natural environment and organizes laughter with an intention to correct, instruct, and readapt individuals to society rather than aiming at the disinterested revelation of pure reality that other arts pursue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat laughter as a social remedy (e.g., neutralizing vanity and separatist tendencies). Unlike 'pure' art which seeks individual revelation, comedy intentionally targets social conventions and aims to 'round off the corners' of rigidities for sociability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation for comedy must be external and general (inductive method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic observation is outward, skin-deep, and inductive: it focuses on surface features and commonalities among people rather than deep inward psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penetrate too far into personality or couple outer effects with very deep causes—doing so risks losing the laughable. Comic method resembles the inductive sciences: compare analogous cases, extract an essence, and form general categories usable on stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic features are unconscious/ invisible to their owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic ever partakes of the unconscious: the laughable trait must be invisible or unconscious to its actual owner while remaining visible to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the character unaware of what makes them ridiculous; if the person recognizes their own failing the comic effect is weakened. This invisibility allows laughter to function as an external corrective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of an ideal comic type
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal comic type should be deep-rooted yet superficial; invisible to its owner; visible to everyone else; extremely self-considerate; troublesome to others; immediately repressible; recurrent under fresh aspects; inseparable from social life; and capable of being attached to various vices or virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing comic types, ensure these properties so the type supplies inexhaustible matter while remaining within comedy's scope. The combination allows repeated and varied instances of the same comic essence without losing laughability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity as a primary source of the comic
rubrics_metrics.description: Vanity is singled out as a ubiquitous mixture that is both superficial and deep-rooted — 'the one failing that is essentially laughable' — and is both widespread and resistant to simple moral correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use manifestations of vanity (self-admiration based on supposed admiration from others) as fertile comic material. Laughter is presented as the specific remedy for vanity, and comedy often seeks to expose and neutralize vanity's social inconvenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional comic: exploit profession-specific habits, solemnity, callousness and jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain professions form small societies with shared habits of mind (professional vanity, callousness, specialized jargon and logic) that make their members resemble each other and hence are ripe for comic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters apply professional language or reasoning to ordinary life (e.g., doctors treating ordinary affairs as if made for medicine) to produce ludicrous effects; this device can be coarse but becomes refined if combined with personal peculiarities (examples: Molière's doctors; Regnard's Joueur).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional logic / comic logic: localized reasoning that appears absurd to common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic effects often arise from a kind of logic valid within a particular circle but absurd or inapplicable to common experience; this is a distinctive, localized form of 'absurdity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create situations where a character's internal, profession- or obsession-driven reasoning yields conclusions that clash with universal/common-sense logic. Emphasize the contrast between particular and universal logic to produce comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdity in comedy is a specific inversion of common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic's absurdity is not general absurdity but a particular inversion: attempting to mould things to an idea in one's mind rather than molding one's ideas to things (Don Quixote seeing giants where others see windmills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for absurd situations that reveal a fixed privileged recollection or idea 'waiting' to be embodied in perception; avoid merely random or indefinite absurdity, as it will often fail to be funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition and multiple exemplars to establish a comic type
rubrics_metrics.description: To define a comic 'species' the comic poet shows several different copies/varieties of the same model (satellites around a central character), much as a naturalist enumerates varieties to define a species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage or narrate multiple characters who share the defining traits of a type to make the generality manifest and increase the scope for varied comic situations.
